dharana.numbering_edition: Jaideva Singh 1979 (dhāraṇā 1 = verse 24; dhāraṇā 82 = verses 105–106 and dhāraṇā 89 = verses 113–114, otherwise one verse each; dhāraṇā 112 = verse 137)
dharana.sanskrit_iast: bhayā sarvaṃ ravayati sarvado vyāpako 'khile | iti bhairavaśabdasya santatoccāraṇāc chivaḥ ||
dharana.sanskrit_source: GRETIL e-text, compared with Wallis's concordance, Pradīpaka and the Singh scan
dharana.rendering: 'By radiance (bhā) he makes everything resound (ravayati), he gives all (sarvada), he pervades (vyāpaka) the whole': thus, by continuously sounding the word 'Bhairava', one becomes Śiva.
dharana.rendering_attribution: School paraphrase drawing on Jaideva Singh (1979), Christopher Wallis and Bettina Bäumer (as printed in Wallis's concordance); not a quotation.
dharana.commentary_note: Singh gives several traditional etymologies of 'Bhairava': bhā (the light of consciousness) + ai (the power of action) + rava (comprehending); Abhinavagupta's 'he who supports the cosmos and sounds the great mantra I (aham)'; bha-ra-va as maintenance, withdrawal and projection of the universe. He insists that uccāra here is not mechanical repetition but the sounding of the inner life-force (prāṇa-śakti) rising from the heart to the dvādaśānta. Singh classes it as śāktopāya. Wallis notes there are up to five ways to translate the verse.
dharana.instruction: Softly and steadily sound 'Bhairava', aloud or silently, remembering its meaning.

checked_against: Jaideva Singh 1979 (scanned copy): '[Dhāraṇā 105] VERSE 130'. OCR note: Singh's heading is OCR'd as '[Dhāraṇā lOS]' (105).
The Mystery Within (2019), Session Two list: 'Dharana 105' = verse 130 (agrees with Singh)
Wallis concordance: verse 130 = 'The word ‘Bhairava’ (Y105 ~ B3)' (verse text and technique match)
GRETIL, Wallis and Pradīpaka: Sanskrit of verse 130 compared
verification.notes: Door index = Singh dhāraṇā number, read directly in Singh's own headings and cross-checked against The Mystery Within's Singh-numbered list and Wallis's concordance. Caveat: Singh was read from an OCR scan, not a print copy in hand.

numbering_variants.mystery_within_parallel: The parallel-translations section of The Mystery Within labels verse 130 'Dharana 107', because from verse 106 on it gives every verse its own number (106 = 83 … 137 = 114). Singh and the same book's Session Two list put this at dhāraṇā 105. Not followed.

source_disagreements: Singh reads uccāraṇa as the inner rising of the life-force (prāṇa-śakti) from the heart to the dvādaśānta, not spoken repetition; Wallis renders 'constantly utters'. The door teaches soft sounding, aloud or silent, and does not teach directing the life-force.
The etymology in the verse is read in several ways (Wallis: 'up to five ways to translate this verse'); the paraphrase follows the shared core: radiance, resounding, giving, pervading.

seat.label: Any steady, comfortable position (school addition)
seat.summary: Any steady, comfortable position: sitting on a chair, sitting on the floor with support under the hips, or lying on the back. Standing or walking slowly is also acceptable when that is easier. Choose the position in which the body needs the least effort.
seat.honesty: School addition. Verse 130 does not specify a body position. The seat is a convenience so the dharana can be practised; it is not part of the technique and makes no claim of tradition.

points: its meaning: radiance, resounding, giving, pervading
geometry.summary: Not a body shape. The map is one word, 'Bhairava', sounded steadily, with its meaning (radiance that makes everything resound, gives all and pervades all) carried in the sound.
geometry.svg_hint: three syllables in a row with soft rings spreading out from them
geometry.honesty: Geometry records the dharana's own map of attention, not a body shape. Locations marked 'commentarial' come from commentary, not from the verse.

reaction.name: Let the name resound
reaction.summary: School metaphor only: a single sacred word is sounded continuously, with its meaning, until the sounding itself becomes the meaning. Not a biochemical or medical claim.

breath.lands_in: the soft, steady sound of the name
breath.cue: Natural breath. Sound 'Bhairava' softly on the out-breath or silently. A free breath whenever you need it. No forced hold.
breath.honesty: The counts are an optional school pacing aid, not part of the verse. Hold is always 0: this school never adds a deliberate breath-hold.

orientation.cue: Sound the name softly and steadily, remembering its meaning
orientation.gravity: Let the floor or chair carry the body completely; there is no posture to hold
orientation.degrees_hint: No angle target: the VBT gives no posture for this dharana

attention.primary: The sound 'Bhairava', soft and continuous, aloud or silent
attention.secondary: Its meaning: radiance that makes everything resound, gives all and pervades all

adiyogi.verse_paraphrase: 'By radiance (bhā) he makes everything resound (ravayati), he gives all (sarvada), he pervades (vyāpaka) the whole': thus, by continuously sounding the word 'Bhairava', one becomes Śiva.
adiyogi.method_summary: Recall the meaning: radiance that makes everything resound, that gives all, that pervades all. Then sound 'Bhai-ra-va' softly and steadily, aloud or in the mind, with that meaning in the sound, not as a mechanical repetition.

honesty.disclosure: Door 105 follows Vijñāna Bhairava Tantra dharana 105 (verse 130) in Jaideva Singh's numbering. The door-to-dharana index is a School of 112 Doorways teaching device. Singh's sequence is one edition's count, not an ancient one-to-one canon. The seat, counts, reaction and beat scripts are school additions.
honesty.notes: pairing_type is school_device: the dharana is the content, while the door index, seat and pacing are the school's.
flags: Door index = Jaideva Singh dharana number: Door 105 is dharana 105, verse 130. Other editions number differently (see dharana.numbering_variants).
The seat, breath counts, reaction metaphor, attention-map drawing and beat scripts are school devices, not part of the verse.
The English is a school paraphrase, not a quotation from any translator.
No medical claims. Reaction names are metaphors, not biochemistry.

safety.pain_rule: Pain is information. Pause, regress, or exit. Never push through sharp pain.
safety.open_seat_alternate: This door needs no particular posture: sit on a chair, sit on the floor with support, or lie down. Eyes may stay open.
safety.contraindication_notes: General practice caution only; not medical advice. Keep the voice soft and the breath natural; rest whenever the throat or breath tires. If anything feels distressing (dizziness, agitation, strong emotion), stop, open the eyes and rest attention on the feet and the floor.
